draft.title: Transport connecting people to goods
card: Transport moves people and goods from one place to another. This connects people to things they need, such as food, fuel and medicine, even when those things are made far away.
Trucks and vans move goods door to door and can reach almost any town. They are flexible, but they carry smaller loads than trains or ships.
Trains haul heavy loads, such as grain, coal and containers, over long distances on fixed tracks.
Ships carry very large loads between countries at a low cost for each item, but slowly. Planes are fast but cost more, so they suit light, high-priced or perishable goods.
draft.remember: Each type of transport suits different goods, and together they connect places to what people need.

a.q: Why are ships widely used to carry goods between countries?
opts: They carry very large loads at a low cost for each item
They are the fastest way to move goods between countries
They can deliver goods straight to any house or shop
They run on fixed tracks that link every large town
a.why: Ships carry huge loads, so the cost for each item is low, even though they are slow. The fastest option is a plane, not a ship, which makes the speed answer tempting but wrong.
a.clue: Think about size of load and cost, not speed.

b.q: Priya runs a flower shop in Orange. Fresh roses must reach her from a farm in Colombia within a few days. Which transport suits this best, and why?
opts: Planes, because they are fast and roses spoil quickly
Ships, because they carry roses at the lowest cost
Railways, because trains run on fixed tracks to Orange
Roads, because trucks can cross the ocean to the farm
b.why: Roses are perishable, so speed matters more than low cost. Planes are fast, so they suit this case. Ships are cheaper, but they are too slow and the roses would spoil before arriving.
b.clue: Fresh flowers spoil quickly, so what matters most?

a.best: They carry very large loads at a low cost for each item
